Label: p2evalbrief. Read /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8dd13422-fd1a-523f-85e2-4beea8788ff6/scratchpad/brief-common.md first; it binds you.
Worktree: G /home/user/wt-g-p2evalbrief (cloud/p2evalbrief). Do not edit vendored modules (report if needed).

1. P2-7 `shell-payload-quoting-corrupted-data` (3x; ledger counter wrongly reads 4x because one incident was captured twice). Incident: `'...\worktrees\$n...'` reached PowerShell as `worktrees$n` and created a stray junction. Decide the owner: eval-guard already owns "no inline payloads; write a file" — extend it (no new guard) unless the evidence shows another owner. Rule: inside a `powershell -Command`/`pwsh -c`/`cmd /c` argument built in an outer shell, a backslash that the outer shell would consume (adjacent to `$`, or any backslash inside bash double quotes) is refused with the file recipe. Use the shared shell-command parser's view of quoting. Incident payload first in the selftest; near-misses: single-quoted payload without expansion, a .ps1 file invocation, forward-slash paths. Fix the counter through `failure-capture/capture.mjs` (read its usage; supersede/dismiss as appropriate); if it has no write-free `--dry-run`, add one (selftest + mutants) — never hand-edit the ledger.
2. P2-9: brief-feasibility lets a worker brief through that asks for `git switch`/`checkout`; only worker-git-guard stops it at run time. One decision, two call sites: export worker-git-guard's deny predicate (no behaviour change; its campaign is being measured in another frozen tree — keep its decision code byte-identical where possible, re-point mutant targets only if you must move code) and have brief-feasibility import it. Parity selftest: every denied command in worker-git-guard's fixtures, placed in a brief, is refused by brief-feasibility. Sibling: refuse an Agent brief that asks a subagent_type with no shell tool (read the agent definition's `tools` frontmatter, e.g. jd-judge-a/b have Read/Glob/Grep only) to run git or npm.
Selftests + mutants for both; mutation-proof scope.

Decision on the worker-git face: not landing at a measured 1 false / 1 true on the 10 real briefs (and it would refuse my own brief). The owner's rule: a new rule lands with zero offenders, or stays registered but not enabled. The root cause is yours to fix, not the face's width: `instructions.mjs` reads any code span without a prohibition word as an ORDER. Make it tell an order from a mention structurally: an order is a command the brief directs the worker to execute (imperative cue in the same clause/line: run/execute/do/use/then/ejecuta/corre/usa…, a "Run:"-style lead-in, or a fenced block under such a lead-in); a mention is a command the brief describes, quotes from an incident, forbids, or names as refused/denied/past ("the incident ran `git update-ref`", "is refused", "never `git switch`", "asks for `git switch`" inside a quotation of another brief). Measure on the 10 real fixture briefs AND on the briefs of this session's agents (they are in this session's transcripts; my brief-common.md and the briefs I sent are good negatives): target 0 false refusals with the true `git commit -m` one still refused. If you cannot reach 0 false with evidence, register the face as advisory (advise, not deny) and say why. Selftests + mutants for the order/mention decision. The other commits (eval-guard, worker-git-guard, recount, ledger recount) I already cherry-picked to master separately, so on your branch rebuild from origin/master: create a fresh branch from origin/master and cherry-pick only your brief-feasibility commits (6dc4eb5 bd3ded5 36a0b84 b394947 6362bbf) plus the new work. Commit, don't push; report the false/true counts.

# Common brief for every worker (read fully before starting)

Repos: G = owner's `~/.claude` (github adrijimcab/claude-global-config, master 9f8c0cf). B = the b100
project's `.claude/` tooling (adrijimcab/b100-am-ui-claude-tooling, master c54afc0). You were given your
own linked worktree(s); write ONLY there and in your private scratch
`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8dd13422-fd1a-523f-85e2-4beea8788ff6/scratchpad/<your-label>/`.
NEVER write in /home/user/wt-frozen-9f8c0cf (a mutant campaign measures it), in the main clones, or in
another worker's worktree. Never push; never touch master. Commit as you go (small conventional commits,
English, no Co-Authored-By/AI attribution). Commit before reporting.

Owner rules that bind you (from the owner's hand-off; read `checklists/master-backlog.md` in G for context):
- Senior architect / CTO standard: root cause, no patches, no suppressions, no exclusions, no thresholds
  without a measured distribution. State what would make your design wrong and prove it with a test.
- Every deciding module has a selftest AND a mutant campaign (`*.mutants.mjs`, mutation-proof engine,
  assertion kills; see neighbours). A new guard's selftest MUST drive the original incident payload.
- Bilingual: code comments/JSDoc and every runtime message English first, then `@es` Spanish (correct
  accents). Follow the style of neighbouring modules exactly; each hook has a `*.hook-registration.json`
  sidecar and is wired through `hook-dispatch/manifests/*.json` or settings.json as its neighbours are.
- Vendored modules (`G/vendored/PROVENANCE.json`: shell-command, agent-liveness, toolchain-guard,
  mutation-proof, write-targets, …) change ONLY at their B source, then are re-synced into G with
  `node vendored/vendored.mjs sync` (its source path is the owner's Windows checkout; in this cloud box
  point it at your B worktree the way the vendored module allows — read its header; if it cannot, copy
  byte-identically and update PROVENANCE hashes exactly as sync would, and say so).
- Lessons ledgers are written ONLY by `failure-capture/capture.mjs` (capture / supersede / dismiss).
- Do NOT run the full chain (`selftest-runner/run.mjs` bare is refused by a guard on the host). Run the
  selftests and mutant campaigns of everything you touched and of every module that imports it (find
  importers with rg), plus `node mutation-proof/scope.mjs` and `node vendored/vendored.mjs check` where
  relevant. Linux container: some selftests are Windows-bound; state which you could not run and why.
- Never `sleep`-poll; redirect long runs to a log in your scratch and read it.
Report: branch, commits, files, design decision + what would make it wrong, exact test evidence
(counts), anything UNVERIFIED, and anything that only the owner's Windows host can do.
